statement: Reading buffered data from a closed stream, when permitted, never reopens it.
close is idempotent, a closed stream stays closed, and buffered data delays eof without making isopen true.

A Timer or AsyncCondition event already pending at close can be observed one final time without reopening the object.

source: base/show.jl:104-135; display-width invariant for limited Dict and Set output
statement: The truncation helper always returns text whose display width is at most the requested positive width.
ANSI-aware truncation does not append a second reset after the last retained delimiter is already a reset.
Nonpositive and mark-too-narrow widths return an empty string, and empty input is padded exactly when requested.
ANSIIterator preserves visible characters, groups ANSI delimiters, assigns them zero width, and exposes the declared iterator traits.
Type-depth limiting ignores braces inside every printable ASCII character literal.
Type-depth limiting handles every printable ASCII character literal except backslash.
A depth limit above the nesting of an unquoted escape-free type string preserves the string.
Relative TextTerminal cursor movement delegates to cmove with the terminal and clamps down and right coordinates to the terminal bounds.
The TextTerminal interface forwards stream queries, position queries, one-step wrappers, and default operations exactly as its method bodies specify.
UnixTerminal cursor and mode operations emit the exact CSI escape sequences and bell byte.
TTY terminal wrappers forward to their streams and properties, and raw mode returns the recorded libuv result.
Core output wrappers target standard output, DevNull reports its fixed behavior, and CoreIO has the documented bootstrap read and write behavior.
A flag-only extended section assigns its flag to the label stored in the names table.
The terminfo reader decodes little-endian fields and resolves present string offsets to NUL-terminated byte sequences.
TermInfo lookup selects the dictionary matching the requested default type, reports membership across dictionaries, and lists each key once.
TermInfo construction combines the declared standard and extended capabilities and applies long aliases.
Terminfo search checks the environment and standard candidate paths in order, and loading returns empty state when no readable file exists.
Terminal color detection follows the environment and capability rules, caches results, and exposes the TTY color property.
IOContext constructors preserve the wrapped stream, add bindings in argument order, and wrappers delegate to the unwrapped stream.
IOContext lookup uses the newest matching binding, while a plain IO has no context keys.
IOContext displaysize uses a valid context override and otherwise delegates to the wrapped stream.
Circular display detects the nearest identical object in the context chain and prints the correct circular-reference marker.
Scalar display uses numeric Bool spelling only under Bool type information, and prints Nothing and signed integers directly.
Hexadecimal unsigned display has the type-width padding and evaluates to the original value.
Decimal unsigned display prints its decimal digits and includes the type suffix only when type information differs.
Pair display chooses typed and arrow forms from type tightness, delimiters, compactness, and type information.
Module display prints a root name or the complete dotted parent path.
The small display wrappers forward, decorate, summarize, or fall back exactly as their method bodies specify.
Default display prints circular markers, assigned and unassigned fields, and raw bits in the specified order.

julia_functions: show_delim_array(::IO, itr, op, delim, cl, delim_one)
statement: Delimited display preserves order, separators, singleton tuple commas, circular markers, and unassigned array slots.
Summary and showarg methods print dimensions, indices, parent arrays, element types, and iterator wrappers according to their specializations.
Bit display emits each stored bit in index order and inserts only the specified spacing.
dump respects maximum depth, limited array windows, one-line specializations, and datatype headers.
Real display aligns immediately before its decimal point or exponent.
A real value without a decimal point or exponent places its full width left of the alignment point.
Alignment wrappers split rational and complex components, preserve total pair width, and suppress color during measurement.
Function display distinguishes intrinsic, built-in, generic, global, compact, and fallback cases, and active_module selects Main or the active REPL module.
Key, value, and dictionary text display handles empty, circular, limited, truncated, aligned, and ellipsis cases in source order.
Type-alias analysis collects referenced modules and free variables, removes binder bounds for matching, reapplies context binders, and returns one most-specific valid alias.

Real classification agrees with a nonzero decomposition denominator, for independently typed numerator and exponent components.
Every Integer subtype, including unbounded integers, is finite, non-NaN and non-infinite under its exact decomposition.
Floating parity agrees with divisibility of the exact Integer value, including the large-even-integer shortcut and nonintegral rejection.

Radix precision rejects bases below two and returns the integer exponent bracketing 2^binaryPrecision between successive powers of the requested base, assuming the logarithm-floor callee satisfies that numeric contract.
All ten signed and unsigned BitInteger types convert to each IEEE format by nearest rounding with ties to even; AbstractFloat selects the same correctly-rounded Float64 conversion.
Every finite narrowing conversion is nearest-even rounding of the exact rational input; infinities keep their sign and NaNs remain NaN.
Every Integer representation has a nonzero denominator and reconstructs its mathematical integer value exactly.
Every abstractly-typed array is rejected with ErrorException; successful concrete-array conversion preserves the elementwise floating analog required by the convert interface.
Floatmin is the smallest positive normal value, and floatmax is the greatest finite value, in every IEEE format.
Machine epsilon has exact value 2^(-significand_bits), and adding it to one produces the least representable value greater than one.

All mixed equality, strict-order, and non-strict-order methods compare exact mathematical values in both argument orders for all Float16/32/64 bit patterns and all ten BitInteger types; every comparison with NaN is false.

Equality, strict ordering, and non-strict ordering between every Float32/Float64 bit pattern and every Int64/UInt64/Int128/UInt128 value compare their exact mathematical values in both argument orders; NaN comparisons are false.
Every UInt128 and Int128 converts to Float16, Float32, and Float64 by IEEE 754 nearest rounding with ties to even, across its complete integer domain.
Every UInt128 converts to Float64 by IEEE 754 nearest rounding with ties to even, including both exponent-packing branches and their sticky low bits.
Every Int128 converts to Float64 by IEEE 754 nearest rounding with ties to even, including typemin(Int128) and both signs.
Every Int128 converts to Float32 by IEEE 754 nearest rounding with ties to even, including typemin(Int128), both signs, and exponent carries.
Every UInt128 converts to Float32 by IEEE 754 nearest rounding with ties to even, including carry into the next exponent and overflow to positive infinity.

For every IEEEFloat format (Float16, Float32, Float64), isless and isequal partition all bit patterns into a strict total order on isequal classes, with -0.0 strictly before +0.0 and all NaNs in one top class.
For every IEEEFloat format (Float16, Float32, Float64), isless is transitive across every triple of bit patterns, including signed zeros and NaN payloads.
Base.uabs(x) returns the exact non-negative magnitude |x| as an unsigned integer of the same bit width for every BitInteger x, avoiding signed overflow at typemin(T).

Every integer of a BitInteger type whose bit width does not exceed the target IEEEFloat significand precision, as well as Bool, converts exactly to a finite IEEEFloat with that integer's rational value.
==, <, and <= between Float16/Float32/Float64 and every BitInteger type of at most 32 bits, in both argument orders, compare the exact mathematical values; NaN compares false.

For every IEEEFloat format Tf and BitInteger type Ti, round(Ti, x, RoundToZero) returns the exact integer truncation toward zero when x is finite and in Ti's range and throws InexactError(:round) otherwise; unsafe_trunc agrees on all in-range inputs.

For every IEEEFloat format Tf and BitInteger type Ti, Ti(x) returns the exact integer value when x is a finite integral value in Ti's range and throws InexactError otherwise; Bool(x::Float16) accepts ±0.0 and 1.0 and throws InexactError(:Bool) otherwise.

For every IEEEFloat format and BitInteger step d, nextfloat(x, d) and prevfloat(x, d) equal |d| iterative applications of single-step nextfloat/prevfloat, and single-step nextfloat/prevfloat produce the adjacent IEEEFloat value with no float strictly between.

For Float16, Float32, and Float64, sign_mask, exponent_mask, and significand_mask are disjoint and partition all bits; exponent/significand metadata match IEEE 754 parameters; mantissa extracts the significand bits; and reinterpret round-trips with integer bit patterns.

ieee754_representation packs sign, biased exponent, and significand into the exact IEEE 754 bit pattern, and its :omega, :nan, :inf, :subnormal, and :zero overloads produce ±floatmax, quiet/payload NaNs, ±Inf, subnormals, and ±0.0.

isnan, isinf, and isfinite match the IEEE 754 exponent/significand classification, and decompose(x) returns (0,0,0) for NaN, (±1,0,0) for ±Inf, and (num, pow, ±1) for finite floats such that x equals (num/den) * 2^pow.

Widening conversions between Float16, Float32, and Float64 preserve exact rational order; promote_rule and widen select the wider IEEEFloat type; and 128-bit integer-to-float conversions handle zero, sign, and two-part/top-bit mantissa reconstruction.
IEEE ==, <, and <= return false whenever either operand is NaN, equate -0.0 and +0.0, and form a strict total order on non-NaN values up to signed-zero equality.

IEEEFloat round modes preserve non-finite and zero inputs, round finite non-zero values by truncated/floored/ceiled integer quotients with sign preservation, and _round_convert adjusts converted integers by one ulp according to rounds_up.

Unary - flips the sign bit and preserves magnitude on non-NaN floats, abs clears the sign bit, NaN operands propagate through +, -, *, /, and muladd, and invalid forms Inf - Inf, Inf * 0, 0 / 0, and Inf / Inf yield NaN.

unbiased_exponent extracts the raw exponent field, explicit_mantissa_noinfnan sets the hidden leading bit iff the float is not subnormal, _to_float reconstructs normalized floats, rem and mod return NaN on infinite dividends, zero divisors, or NaN inputs; finite dividends smaller than the divisor are unchanged by rem, equal magnitudes give signed zero, and infinite divisors preserve finite dividends.

precision returns 11, 24, and 53 for Float16, Float32, and Float64 and rejects bases below 2 with DomainError; issubnormal, ispow2, iseven, isodd, typemin, typemax, floatmin, floatmax, and eps satisfy their IEEE 754 boundary and unit-in-last-place invariants.

bswap on IEEEFloat reverses the byte order of the underlying unsigned bit pattern as an involution, and float on arrays and ranges converts concrete elements or range endpoints while rejecting abstractly-typed arrays with ErrorException.

On declared parameterless types and their unions (each type name declared once), typejoin(T, S) returns a supertype of both that is a subtype of every declared common supertype: their closest common ancestor.
typejoin of zero inputs is Union{}, one input is unchanged, and typejoin returns every type other than a type variable when joined with itself.
For every pair of primitive numeric types, typejoin returns their closest common ancestor in the numeric type hierarchy.
For unions of simple types, typesplit(a, b) is a subtype of a, and Union{typesplit(a, b), b} == Union{a, b}.
On declared types and their unions, promote_typejoin(T, S) returns a supertype of both T and S, which is equivalent to typejoin(T, S) when neither contains Nothing or Missing.

The type R returned by promote_op(f, S...) satisfies f(args...) isa R for all args isa S, given that inference bounds f's result type; for a Union{} argument type it is Union{}, which no call can reach.
